podcast.body: This groundbreaking song is notable for its extensive and exaggerated use of the Auto-Tune effect, pushing it to its maximum setting to create a distinctive "robotic sound." "Believe" was instrumental in popularizing Auto-Tune not merely as a subtle pitch correction tool, but as a prominent and overt artistic effect, subsequently influencing numerous artists to explore its creative capabilities. "But then along came Share and the song Believe in 1998, in which the auto-tune effect was maxed out, resulting in this robotic sound."

podcast.body: This number one hit from a 52-year-old Cher spent four weeks atop the Hot 100 and is notable for being the song that introduced Auto-Tune to the masses. Its distinctive "wobbling voice" was the result of a studio accident that Cher insisted be kept in the mix, subsequently altering the sound of pop for the following decade. "It was the song that broke auto tune for The Masses. Thanks to a studio accident that Share demanded be left in the mix, this song's wobbling voice changed the sound of pop for the next decade."
